In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Commentary on Surat al-'Asr

It is Makkan.

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿By al-'Asr. Indeed, mankind﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: It is time (ad-dahr), and in it is a lesson, in that the night and the day pass in one fixed order.

It is reported from al-Hasan and Qatadah that it is the late afternoon (al-'ashiy).

The poet said:

(He set out with us, 'Amr, when the afternoon had grown short ... and in the first setting out lies reward and recompense)

The "'asran" (the two 'asrs) are the night and the day; it is also said that they are the morning and the evening.

Muqatil said: Al-'Asr is the 'Asr prayer.

It is reported from some of them that it is the era of the Prophet, by which He swore. It is also related that in the reading (harf) of 'Ali: "By al-'Asr and the misfortunes of time, indeed mankind is in loss, and he remains in it until the end of life."

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: by the Lord of al-'Asr.

His statement: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ means: in deprivation (ghabn). It is also said: in evil; and it is said: in ruin. Loss (khusran) is the disappearance of the capital, and the capital of the human being is his life and his self; so when he disbelieves, his capital is gone. "Mankind" here is the disbeliever. It is also said that it is a singular with the meaning of a plural. And it is said that it refers to one particular disbeliever; some said that he was Ubayy ibn Khalaf, some said al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and some said Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

And His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ meaning: with acts of obedience.

And His saying: ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ — al-Hasan and Qatadah said: that is, to the Qur'an and following it. It was also said: to tawhid (the oneness of God).

From as-Suddi: "to God," that is, they enjoin one another to God. And from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: they urge one another to obedience to God.

And His saying: ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ — in refraining from acts of disobedience. It was also said: patience in obedience. A strange report has come down, narrated by Abu Umamah, that His saying ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ refers to Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

And His saying ﴿Except those who believe﴾ refers to Abu Bakr; ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ refers to 'Umar; ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ refers to 'Uthman; ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ refers to 'Ali, may God be pleased with them.
